messages:
liz_cs: FYI - ACME integration is failing when the model emits a tool call. Our compat layer throws a SchemaValidationError about the status enum. Customer sent a repro.

liz_cs: raw model response the customer sent (redacted IDs):
```
{
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "process_order",
    "arguments": "{\"order_id\": 1234, \"status\": \"ok\", \"result\": \"{\\\"items\\\":[{\\\"sku\\\":\\\"X12\\\",\\\"qty\\\":1}]}\"}"
  }
}
```

daniel_support: can you paste the exact compat-layer error from our logs?

liz_cs: Logs: `SchemaValidationError: /tool_call/arguments/status value "ok" is not one of ["SUCCESS", "FAILURE"]`
Also when we try to decode arguments we see: `JSONParsingError: Unexpected token { in string at position 0` — so args is a string containing JSON (stringified JSON) + status casing mismatch.

maria_eng_ml: two separate problems: 1) enum casing mismatch (model returned lowercase "ok" instead of canonical enum) and 2) arguments is double-encoded (string containing JSON). Are they using OpenAI tool_call or are they synthesizing JSON in free text?

liz_cs: customer says they're using the model's tool call feature. They POST to our hosted endpoint like this: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"process order 1234"}],"features":{"tool_calling":true}}'
```

ryan_eng_runtime: can you include the inference id + raw bytes? I'll check the normalizer and parser.

liz_cs: inference_id: `inf_2024_09_12_7a3b` — raw payload attached above (same as earlier). Full raw response had finish_reason: `tool_call` and tool_call.arguments as a JSON string.

ryan_eng_runtime: ok — short term we can: 1) relax enum validation to accept common lowercase variants (ok/failed) and map to canonical SUCCESS/FAILURE, and 2) attempt to detect and auto-parse stringified JSON in arguments if it's valid JSON. I'll schedule a canary patch for the compat normalizer.

daniel_support: i'll ask ACME for the exact prompt + any prompt engineering they're doing and share. adding repro steps to the ticket now.

acme_integration: we tried forcing the model with an example response, but sometimes the model wraps nested objects in a string. is there a recommended prompt or flag?

maria_eng_ml: best-practice prompt: be absolutely explicit about response shape, show an exact example, and include: "Respond with a single JSON object and do not wrap nested JSON in strings." If using tool_calling, prefer letting the model emit `tool_call` with `arguments` as an object. Example: 
```json
{
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "process_order",
    "arguments": {
      "order_id": 1234,
      "status": "SUCCESS",
      "result": { "items": [{"sku":"X12","qty":1}] }
    }
  }
}
```

ryan_eng_runtime: for a temporary workaround we can also add a request-side transformation: when `features.response_format=structured-v1` is set we can attempt auto-coercion. i'll open a runtime ticket and include logs + expected behavior. ETA: canary in 24-48h, full rollout after QA.

liz_cs: thanks — i'll update ACME with both the prompt guidance and the temporary workaround (configure `response_format=structured-v1`). will keep this escalated until runtime patch is live. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deploy job #4567 for compat-normalizer at 2024-09-13T02:00Z (watch for regression alerts).

maria_eng_ml: one more note — we should add a small validation utility to our docs for customers: example bad vs good model outputs, and common gotchas (enum casing, stringified args). i'll draft a short doc and link it in the support reply.

liz_cs: perfect. tagging this as escalated -> eng-runtime. i'll post updates here once ACME confirms workaround works.
